goal: The existing Next.js frontend is a presentation shell over the existing FastAPI adapter and backend service. RAG chat, verification and dataset generation have separate pages. The screens follow the user's recorded choices and render structured, readable results. Verification shows automatic saved-review history and scannable task and retrieval views. Streamlit remains removed.
out: Changing retrieval, generation, budget, gold, sealed evaluation or release decision logic beyond exposing existing service calls and read-only saved-review history
Adding another API or frontend stack beyond the existing Next.js frontend and FastAPI adapter, or restoring Streamlit
Adding login or authentication (Phase 3 decision: no login)
Copying the repository or creating another checkout for this task
Merging the pull request or claiming dataset acceptance before the user confirms it
done: DESIGN.md records the user's concrete choices for navigation and page split, chat claims with E1/E2 citations and source preview, verification trace and review layout, dataset generation and candidate review, every original UI setting or control, typography and density, and accessible colours. The recorded alternatives cover at least three navigation, chat, verification, dataset and palette variants. Existing accepted choices are retained rather than reopening the abandoned Streamlit decision.

DESIGN.md records the current Next.js design pass in order: purpose and layout, browser-measured widths/spacing/button behaviour, typography, user-selected accessible colours, remaining space. Historical Streamlit measurements and fixture observations are clearly distinguished from current measurements on the real runtime.

RAG chat, verification and dataset generation are separate Next.js pages at /, /verify/ and /dataset/, served through the existing API. Chat has no evaluation, trace or debug controls. Verification holds retrieval trace, run comparison, evaluation and release results, original review, development gold review and permitted sealed status.

The dataset page calls the existing source-bound gpt-6-luna draft, submit and decide service functions through the API. Drafting goes through the budget gateway with an estimate and explicit paid consent. Pending candidates appear beside their original evidence spans. A reviewer other than the drafter approves or rejects with a note; self-approval is refused by the service, and sealed questions and labels never reach development generation or the candidate UI.

Frontend domain actions call the typed API client, and API domain actions call service.py. Retrieval, generation, store and budget logic stay behind the service boundary; tests confirm api.py imports no package internals other than service and cover logic exposed by this task. The committed OpenAPI schema matches the adapter. Streamlit app.py and ui.py remain absent.

Results render as structured components: numbered claims with citation chips, labelled status badges, tables and expandable exact evidence. Loading, complete, insufficient-evidence, clarification, conflict, budget-blocked and technical-error states each have a distinct rendering. Verification tasks use a searchable queue beside one selected finding; retrieval stages expose structured stage details and warnings. Revision history reads saved source reviews and development gold decisions automatically without a second manual record form; legacy rejection reasons remain visible, prior unapplied proposals are labelled, and sealed content is excluded.

Controls marked remove in DESIGN.md are absent from the UI; controls marked move-to-CLI remain available through their CLI operations. Settings still used by the backend are retained. The manual verification revision-record form is removed; saving an actual review is sufficient for its history entry.

Accessibility basics hold on the current frontend: Korean UI labels, labelled inputs, keyboard navigation, visible focus and readable contrast. Answer text, exact evidence, task titles and source names use the accepted 16 px reading size; desktop and 390 px layouts keep the page within the viewport, with wide tables scrolling inside their containers. Production build, TypeScript, relevant lint and focused service/API tests pass. Fixture tests establish contracts, not real-answer quality or user visual acceptance.

The user has clicked through chat, verification and dataset generation on the actual corpus and runtime and explicitly confirmed each screen before the overall done report. Chat and verification acceptance are recorded; dataset acceptance remains pending until confirmed. The user's later recovery request authorizes committing and opening a PR while that acceptance remains pending. No acceptance is inferred from a synthetic provider response, a smoke test or an agent's own browser inspection. Paid provider calls require explicit consent.

decisions.what: Continue the existing Next.js frontend and FastAPI adapter over service.py; keep Streamlit removed
decisions.why: The user explicitly abandoned Streamlit because of limited layout flexibility. The current branch already contains the selected replacement and the three working pages.
decisions.rejected: Restoring Streamlit or creating another frontend/API implementation to satisfy the obsolete stack requirement

decisions.what: Retain the concrete design choices recorded in DESIGN.md and inspect the actual rendered screens when repairing readability
decisions.why: The user already selected layouts and colours, accepted chat, then required repeated visual inspection and repair of verification. Repeating those choices would reverse settled decisions.
decisions.rejected: Choosing a fresh layout or palette without the user, treating historical fixture screenshots as current acceptance, or claiming zero slop from an unmeasured percentage

decisions.what: Derive revision history automatically from actual saved reviews and decisions
decisions.why: A verifier should perform the review once. Asking for a separate manual revision record duplicates work and does not reliably describe saved outcomes.
decisions.rejected: Requiring copied IDs, quotes and proposal JSON in a second revision-record form

decisions.what: Keep one local task branch and one service/API boundary; preserve backend decision and budget safeguards
decisions.why: The user requested work in branches without repository copies. The existing linked worktree is the assigned workspace, and UI improvements do not require another implementation of backend rules.
decisions.rejected: Another repository copy or worktree, a second service implementation, new login, or paid test calls without consent

decisions.what: Preserve explicit three-page user acceptance and publish the recovered work under the user's direct authorization
decisions.why: The user explicitly transferred commit and PR publication to the assistant after the task server failed to publish. Chat and verification are accepted; dataset acceptance remains outstanding and is disclosed in the PR.
decisions.rejected: Marking all criteria passed because the branch is committed, claiming dataset acceptance, or continuing to enforce server-only publication after the user's explicit recovery instruction
